segments.text: PCRE2-backed; `--static` linking works (verified on Linux, including a Docker `scratch` container — `docker/Dockerfile.regexp-test`). Full design: [TDD-00035](../tdd/TDD-00035.md) ([ADR-00114](../adr/ADR-00114.md)–[ADR-00120](../adr/ADR-00120.md)).

Matching follows the **ECMAScript dialect by default** ([TDD-00067](../tdd/TDD-00067.md), [ADR-00206](../adr/ADR-00206.md)–[ADR-00208](../adr/ADR-00208.md); verified on Apple Silicon, pcre2 10.47). The whole-program `-regex=<mode>` flag selects fidelity: `ecmascript` (default — `es-unicode` matching plus a source-normalization pass, which rewrites `.` to ECMAScript's exact "any character except a line terminator" so it matches `\x0b`/`\x0c`/`\x85` as real JS does), `es-unicode` (`PCRE2_UTF` code-point matching + `NEWLINE_ANY`, no normalization), `es-utf16` (`es-unicode` matching plus true UTF-16 code-unit positions at every user-visible offset — `str.search`'s return, `lastIndex`, a replace callback's `offset` — instead of the byte offsets the rest of the string layer uses), `es-ascii` (the option-level fixes only, byte matching — smallest/fastest for known-ASCII programs), or `pcre` (raw PCRE2/Perl semantics, no ES wrapping — an explicit opt-in for PCRE-only features, *not* a fallback). The `ecmascript` normalization pass covers only the `.` rewrite so far; the remaining sub-items (`\u{…}`/`\p{…}`, Unicode `\w`/`\s`/`\b`, Annex-B legacy octal escapes, exact `$`/`m`) are deferred and disclosed in Known limitations below.

caveats: Does not validate the *flags* string at all — a duplicate flag (`"gg"`) or an unrecognized flag character (`"z"`) is silently accepted instead of throwing `SyntaxError` like real JS ([ADR-00166](../adr/ADR-00166.md))
notes: Compiles the pattern once via `pcre2_compile_8`; throws a real, catchable `SyntaxError` on an invalid *pattern*
A `\uXXXX`/`\xXX` escape compiles as an ECMAScript escape in the default/`es-ascii` modes (`PCRE2_ALT_BSUX`) — see [TDD-00067](../tdd/TDD-00067.md)

caveats: `x in /foo/` mis-lexes the `/` as division (the lexer's regex-vs-division disambiguation gap, since `in` isn't its own token in this lexer) — a small, deliberately-accepted gap
notes: Desugars to the same construction at parse time — see [ADR-00114](../adr/ADR-00114.md)
Plain field reads, original constructor arguments verbatim
Decomposed from the flags string once at construction — no method needs to re-parse it

Mutated by `.exec()`/`.test()`/global `str.match()`/`str.matchAll()`/`str.replace()`/`str.replaceAll()` (advances on a successful `g`-flagged match, resets to `0` after a failed one) — see [ADR-00116](../adr/ADR-00116.md)/[ADR-00117](../adr/ADR-00117.md)/[ADR-00118](../adr/ADR-00118.md)/[ADR-00526](../adr/ADR-00526.md)
Deliberately untouched by `str.split()`/`str.search()`, matching real JS ([ADR-00119](../adr/ADR-00119.md): `.search()` explicitly saves/restores it; `.split()` never reads or writes it at all)

A `g`-flagged RegExp reads/advances `.lastIndex` exactly as `.exec()` does, so `while (re.test(s))` steps through every match; a non-global RegExp always matches from offset 0 and never touches `.lastIndex` — see [ADR-00115](../adr/ADR-00115.md)/[ADR-00526](../adr/ADR-00526.md)

caveats: An unmatched optional capture group becomes `""` rather than a true per-element `null` (no per-element-nullable-string array exists)
Real JS's `index`/`input`/`groups` extra properties on the result aren't built
notes: Returns `string[] \| null` — real, working `m !== null`/`if (m)` checks against the result. See [ADR-00116](../adr/ADR-00116.md)

All matching methods route through the one compiled PCRE2 handle, so the `-regex` dialect mode and its Known-limitations dialect caveats apply uniformly here and to `.match`/`.matchAll`/`.replace`/`.replaceAll`/`.split`/`.search`

caveats: Shares `.exec()`'s result-array narrowing (an unmatched optional capture group becomes `""`, not per-element `null`; no `index`/`input`/`groups`)
notes: Without `g`: identical to `regexp.exec(str)`. With `g`: full-match-only strings, `null` (not `[]`) on zero matches — matches real JS exactly. See [ADR-00117](../adr/ADR-00117.md)

caveats: Returns an eager `string[][]`, not a real lazy iterator (no lazy-iteration infrastructure exists anywhere in this compiler)
notes: One `.exec()`-shaped match array per match; throws `TypeError` without `g`. See [ADR-00117](../adr/ADR-00117.md)

caveats: Replacement template supports `$1`-`$9`/`$&`/`$$` only (`` $` ``/`$'` — pre-/post-match text — are out of scope)

The callback form is invoked with a fixed `(match, offset, string)` — real JS's variadic `...capturedGroups` in the middle isn't supported (a callback's arity is fixed at compile time but a pattern's capture count is only known at runtime; a callback declaring more than 3 parameters is a compile-time error)
notes: Replaces the first match without `g`, every match with `g`; the callback runs exactly once per match. See [ADR-00118](../adr/ADR-00118.md)

caveats: Same replacement narrowing as `.replace()` (`$1`-`$9`/`$&`/`$$` only; fixed `(match, offset, string)` callback)
notes: Same replacement rules as `.replace()`; requires the `g` flag, throwing `TypeError` otherwise. See [ADR-00118](../adr/ADR-00118.md)

caveats: Only splits on a non-zero-length match — real JS's more intricate zero-length-match handling isn't replicated (see [ADR-00119](../adr/ADR-00119.md))
Captured groups in the split pattern are never spliced into the result (out of scope from the start)
notes: Finds every match regardless of `g` (its own local search loop, like real JS)

caveats: A plain-string argument falls back to the pre-`RegExp` `.indexOf()`-shaped behavior rather than coercing the string to a RegExp
notes: Always searches from offset 0, restores `.lastIndex` afterward — invisible to later `.exec()`/`.test()` iteration, matching real JS exactly. See [ADR-00119](../adr/ADR-00119.md)

Deferred for the whole feature's V1, not just Stage 0 — see the TDD's flag scope table; `\u{…}` code-point escapes, surrogate handling, Unicode `\p{…}`/class semantics, and strict-syntax validation are Option C

segments.text:
- **No implicit string→RegExp coercion.** Neither `match()`/`matchAll()`/`replace()`/`replaceAll()`/`search()` implicitly coerces a non-`RegExp` argument (a compile-time error instead), unlike real JS.
- **Dialect-mode caveats** (what diverges from ES, per mode — these residuals exclude the matching rows above from Strict Coverage; [TDD-00067](../tdd/TDD-00067.md)/[ADR-00206](../adr/ADR-00206.md)–[ADR-00208](../adr/ADR-00208.md)):
  - **`ecmascript` (default) — `$`/`m` over-exclude three control chars.** `$`/`m` use `PCRE2_NEWLINE_ANY` and anchor at `\x0b`/`\x0c`/`\x85`, where ES does not — exact anchoring needs a further `$`-rewrite (deferred). The normalization pass does **not** yet handle `\u{…}`/`\p{…}` code-point escapes, ES Unicode `\w`/`\s`/`\b` semantics, Annex-B legacy octal escapes, or the `u`/`v` flags.
  - **`es-unicode` (opt-in) — `.`/`$`/`m` over-exclude three rare control characters.** The newline convention is `PCRE2_NEWLINE_ANY`, the closest single PCRE2 convention to ES's exact line terminators `\n \r \u2028 \u2029`, but it additionally treats `\x0b` (VT), `\x0c` (FF), and `\x85` (NEL) as line boundaries — so `.` excludes them and `$`/`m` anchor at them, where ES does not. Use the default `ecmascript` (whose normalization pass fixes `.`) if this matters.
  - **`es-utf16` — offsets diverge from the byte-indexed string layer, by design.** `str.search`/`lastIndex`/replace-callback `offset` report UTF-16 code units, but `.charCodeAt`/`.length`/`.slice` stay byte-indexed (ADR-00028), so a program that feeds an `es-utf16` RegExp offset into `str.slice(...)` over non-ASCII text gets mismatched positions. This is why `es-utf16` is opt-in and not the default. Matching is identical to `es-unicode`, so every `es-unicode` matching caveat applies to it too.
  - **`es-ascii` — `.` matches `\r`.** With no compile context, PCRE2's default newline convention treats only `\n` as the line end, so `.` matches `\r` where ES excludes it. Deliberate: `es-ascii` is defined as option-bits-only. Use the default `es-unicode` (which excludes `\r`) if this matters.
  - **`pcre` — raw PCRE2/Perl semantics throughout.** The PCRE2-vs-ECMAScript divergences the ES modes correct (`$`/newline, unset backref, `\uXXXX` throw) all apply by design in this mode; it exists for PCRE-only features and pattern porting, not ES fidelity.
  - **`es-unicode`/`ecmascript` — `\w`/`\s`/`\b` are not Unicode-aware.** `PCRE2_UCP` is deliberately not enabled: its Unicode-property tables diverge from ECMAScript's (UCP `\s` matches U+180E, dropped as whitespace by ES in Unicode 6.3), and enabling it *lost* net conformance on `built-ins/RegExp`. So `\w`/`\s`/`\b` match the ASCII/PCRE-default set, not ES's Unicode definitions — the ES Unicode class semantics are deferred ([TDD-00067](../tdd/TDD-00067.md)). Code-point `.` (from `PCRE2_UTF`) is unaffected and works.
  - **`u`(nicode) flag still not implemented in any mode.** `es-unicode`'s `PCRE2_UTF` gives it code-point matching, but `\u{…}` code-point escapes, surrogate handling, Unicode `\p{…}`/class semantics, and strict-syntax validation are Option C — the `u`/`y`/`d` flags remain out of scope (see the row above).
